stem: During the preprocedure equipment check, the perioperative nurse observes that the anesthesia workstation repeatedly reports a ventilator malfunction. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Proceed if a manual ventilation bag is present and report the malfunction after the procedure
options.B: Silence the malfunction alert and use the workstation unless the client develops a ventilation problem
options.C: Keep the malfunctioning workstation out of client use, report the problem, and ensure functioning equipment is available before proceeding
options.D: Use the workstation for induction because preprocedure equipment alerts are not clinically important until a client is connected

rationale: NCSBN 2026 places safe equipment use in Safety and Infection Prevention and Control and directs nurses to inspect equipment, facilitate safe use, and remove malfunctioning equipment from the client care area while reporting the problem. Backup manual ventilation does not justify knowingly using malfunctioning equipment, silencing an alert does not correct the hazard, and unresolved malfunctioning equipment should not be used on a client.
educational_objective: When client-care equipment malfunctions during a pre-use check, remove it from client use, report the malfunction, and ensure safe replacement equipment is available before care proceeds.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
source_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Safe Use of Equipment, printed p. 26 (PDF page 30): inspect equipment for safety hazards; facilitate appropriate and safe use; remove malfunctioning equipment from client care area and report the problem
source_claim_supported: NCSBN directly identifies inspection, safe use, and removal/reporting of malfunctioning client-care equipment as entry-level RN safety activities.

blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Safe Use of Equipment, printed p. 26 (PDF page 30)

audit_findings.source_audit: Official NCSBN 2026 Test Plan, Safe Use of Equipment, printed p.26 verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Inspection, safe use, removal and reporting are directly supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Unsafe; backup equipment does not justify known malfunction.
audit_findings.choice_B: Unsafe; silencing does not resolve hazard.
audit_findings.choice_D: Unsafe; malfunctioning equipment should not enter client use.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C removes the hazard before exposure.
